title: US Air Force Evacuates Tankers From RAF Mildenhall Over Iran Threats, EU Sets a $3.4B 2027 Defense Budget, and China Unveils Its GJ-11 Stealth Drone
subhead: At least 12 KC-135 tankers and three CV-22 Ospreys reposition from England as Iran warns European bases are targets; Brussels outlines a $3.4 billion 2027 defense budget while Poland awaits a December ruling on a permanent US base; China showcases the GJ-11 stealth UCAV; and Russian FSB hackers breach Romanian servers.

sections.heading: US Evacuates Tankers From RAF Mildenhall as Iran Threatens European Bases
sections.body:
The US Air Force has repositioned at least 12 KC-135 Stratotanker aerial refueling aircraft and three CV-22 Osprey tiltrotors away from RAF Mildenhall in England over the past 48 hours amid heightened security protocols tied to Iranian threats, The War Zone and M5 Dergi reported. The Precautionary dispersal coincided with CBS News revelations that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved out of his Washington home into secure military base housing due to credible Iranian assassination threats. In Tehran, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned that if Washington initiates fresh strikes, "any military base used to attack Iran would be a legitimate target, regardless of distance," explicitly extending the threat envelope to European installations, Anadolu Agency reported.

Simultaneously, M5 Dergi reported that US Central Command (CENTCOM) is standing up a new task force dubbed Iron Gate to interdict Iranian military hardware and dual-use technology shipments across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, while Saudi civil defense teams recovered debris from intercepted Houthi missiles in Sabuhah village in the Mecca region.
sections.whyItMatters: Dispersing US tanker fleets from British soil and moving a cabinet secretary onto a military base show that Iranian asymmetric and missile threats are actively altering US force protection across both Europe and Washington.

sections.heading: EU Proposes $3.4B 2027 Defense Budget as Poland Nears Deal on Permanent US Base
sections.body:
The European Union has set out a $3.4 billion defense budget for 2027 that expands military funding for Ukraine, Breaking Defense reported, responding to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's appeal last month for at least €70 billion in additional European commitments. On NATO's eastern flank, Warsaw announced that the Pentagon backs plans for a permanent US military base in Poland, with a final site selection expected in December. Polish officials have shortlisted four locations capable of hosting 5,000 US troops and their families and pledged up to $4.4 billion toward supporting infrastructure.

Poland also completed receipt of its final 2026 shipment of South Korean K2 Black Panther tanks and K9 Thunder self-propelled howitzers on November 9, SavunmaSanayiST reported, and reached an agreement with Kyiv to trade Polish MiG-29 fighter jets for Ukrainian counter-drone technology, Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk told M5 Dergi. Separately, NATO Admiral Pierre Vandier told Breaking Defense that the alliance is embedding Ukrainian personnel and unmanned surface vessels as opposing "red teams" in NATO exercises to force faster tactical adaptation.
sections.whyItMatters: Warsaw's $4.4 billion infrastructure pledge for a permanent US garrison and its MiG-29-for-counter-drone swap with Kyiv cement Poland as NATO's primary eastern operational hub.

sections.heading: China Showcases GJ-11 Stealth UCAV as Pentagon Issues $450M in Space Loans
sections.body:
China publicly lifted the veil on its GJ-11 Sharp Sword (Mysterious Dragon) flying-wing stealth unmanned combat aerial vehicle, showcasing its internal strike bays and manned-unmanned teaming capabilities alongside crewed fighters, The War Zone reported. Across the Pacific, the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital finalized three loans totaling $450 million to bolster domestic US space companies before the fiscal deadline, Breaking Defense reported, while defense contractor AeroVironment secured a multi-year indefinite-delivery contract worth up to $940 million—with an initial $315 million order—for an undisclosed US government customer, according to SavunmaSanayiST.

However, allied force modernization faces industrial headwinds: the South China Morning Post reported that Japan's military buildup is being slowed by prolonged delays in US missile deliveries and domestic parts shortages, while Kratos Defense disclosed that unit costs for its XQ-58 Valkyrie tactical drone have risen to between $6 million and $8 million depending on configuration, up from original $2 million targets, M5 Dergi noted.
sections.whyItMatters: Beijing's operational display of the flying-wing GJ-11 increases pressure on US and allied air defenses just as Western attritable drone costs climb and US foreign military sales backlogs slow Japan's rearmament.

sections.heading: Russian FSB Hackers Breach Romanian Servers and UK Arrests US Soldier for Espionage
sections.body:
Hackers linked to Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) quietly compromised a Romanian government agency's servers to exfiltrate emails concerning NATO and European Union policy, a Slovak cybersecurity firm revealed to Defense News. In a separate counterintelligence breach, British police arrested a senior US soldier stationed in the United Kingdom on Tuesday on suspicion of conducting espionage for Russian intelligence, Defense News reported.

To harden northern waters against Russian hybrid operations, the UK-led Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF)—grouping 10 Northern European nations—will sign a new maritime security pact to coordinate naval patrols and protect seabed infrastructure, M5 Dergi reported, while Northrop Grumman confirmed to The War Zone plans to test-fly its Talon Blue collaborative combat aircraft drone from a British Royal Navy aircraft carrier.
sections.whyItMatters: Simultaneous Russian cyber intrusions into Romanian government networks and the arrest of a senior US service member in Britain highlight Moscow's persistent human and digital intelligence reach inside NATO.

sections.heading: CRS Flags Strategic Risks of Trump's 'Golden Dome' Shield as Turkey Weighs Iraq Base Shift
sections.body:
A newly released Congressional Research Service (CRS) report obtained by USNI News examined the strategic stability implications of the Trump administration's proposed Golden Dome next-generation homeland missile defense shield, warning lawmakers that space-based interceptors could prompt adversary nuclear force expansions. On Capitol Hill, following Tuesday's 211-204 procedural vote shelving impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, newly elected Democratic Rep. Zach Dembo—a former Navy JAG who flipped a Kentucky House seat—told The Hill that impeachment talk remains "premature," even as Al Jazeera and Anadolu Agency reported that an Arlington National Cemetery sentinel publicly reprimanded Hegseth's group for making noise at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day.

In the Middle East, Breaking Defense reported that analysts see Turkey's preparation to withdraw forces from a base in northern Iraq as a shift toward joint security coordination between Ankara and Baghdad.
sections.whyItMatters: The CRS assessment of Golden Dome sets the stage for fierce appropriations debates in the new Congress over homeland missile defense costs and nuclear deterrence stability.

bottomLine: The evacuation of US Air Force tankers from RAF Mildenhall and Treasury Secretary Bessent's move onto a military base underscore acute Iranian threat warnings, while Poland's $4.4 billion bid for a permanent US base and China's GJ-11 stealth drone reveal accelerating force posture shifts.
sources: The War Zone, M5 Dergi, CBS News, Anadolu Agency, Breaking Defense, SavunmaSanayiST, Defense News, South China Morning Post, USNI News, The Hill, Al Jazeera
